title: The Car Division Kiichiro Toyoda Started Inside a Loom Works
conflicts: Platt patent money: the International Directory of Company Histories (Encyclopedia.com) says Sakichi gave Kiichiro the whole £100,000 for car research; Toyota's 75-year history says the balance was cut in July 1934 so Platt paid £83,500 in all, and does not tie it to cars. The story gives both, attributed, and does not claim the money paid for the cars. Who was persuaded: Wikipedia says his father (who died in 1930); the Toyota museum says the president, Risaburo Toyoda; the story follows the museum. Capital: tripled to ¥3 million on 29 January 1934 (Toyota), with a further doubling in 1935 (museum, International Directory) not used.
notes: Stance 'complicates': the Epictetus passage (count the dust and sprains, and expect sometimes to be beaten) sits against a story of careful preparation whose first trucks still broke down. Most sources are Toyota's own archive (75-year history and the Toyota Commemorative Museum); the independent ones are the International Directory of Company Histories and HISTORY.com. The repeat screen flagged the Matsushita edition as same-founder but let it through; the episodes are unrelated.
